title: Asymmetric Phase Coalescer: Tenant-weighted Latency-Fairshare for Prefill/Decode
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Our current prefill/decode orchestration slices requests into uniform phases which causes frequent kernel context switches and suboptimal batching for asymmetric workloads (short chat completions vs long generation). Small tenants with bursty low-attention requests are starved by long-running decode-heavy tenants when using pure throughput-first arbitration. Goal: Implement an 'Asymmetric Phase Coalescer' policy that merges compatible prefill/decode microphases opportunistically and applies tenant-weighted latency budgets to preserve fairness for latency-sensitive workloads while preserving overall throughput. This ticket coordinates design, prototype, and rollout for the policy across scheduler, kernel-selection hints, and metrics/dashboarding.
design_decisions: 1) Coalescing heuristic: group microphases when their estimated attention/memory footprint and kernel-affinity match within a configurable threshold (default 15%). 2) Latency budget: each tenant gets a rolling latency SLA budget (ms per 1k tokens) used to bias coalescing (tenants near budget are exempt). 3) Weighting: tenant weight derived from subscription tier + recent tail-latency incidents; weight normalization ensures no tenant >50% influence on batching decisions. 4) Kernel hinting: when coalesced, emit kernel-selection preference tags to runtime to prefer fused-attn kernels or attention-sparse kernels depending on average sequence length. 5) Feature flag & rollout: staged by region with traffic shaping and canary at 5/20/50% with rollback thresholds defined by error and latency gates.
implementation_plan: - Spike (2d): simulator extension to model coalescing heuristics and tenant-weighted budgets; run replay of 7 days production traces. - Prototype (5d): implement policy in prefill/decode arbiter with unit tests; add kernel-hint metadata to segment descriptor. - Integration (3d): runtime interprets hint, chooses kernel path; add metric tags. - End-to-end perf run (2d): A/B on staging for 48h. - Rollout (1w): Canary -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with dashboards and automated rollback gates. Feature flag: runtime.asymmetric_phase_coalescer (double-gated: control-plane + per-node).
experiment_results: Simulator replay (7d, global prod snapshot) with default thresholds: - Overall token throughput +9.8% - 95th latency for latency-sensitive tenants improved by 13% (median -6%) - 95th latency for large decode tenants increased by 7% (acceptable within current SLO window) - Kernel switch rate reduced by 21% on average - CPU utilization per node reduced by 11% Observations: benefit most pronounced on mixed-tenant nodes; pure-small-tenant nodes see smaller gains. Monte Carlo sensitivity: increasing coalescing threshold to 25% raises throughput to +13% but increases 95th latency for small tenants beyond acceptable SLO — hence default 15%.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Risk of regressing tail latency for tenants with strict latency budgets if weighting calculation lags; mitigated by conservative default weights and rapid budget decay. - Complexity: additional per-tenant state (rolling budget) increases memory and storage write rate; we cap to active tenant set per node. - Kernel hint mismatch: runtime fallback when hinted kernel unavailable could cause extra latency spikes; add telemetry to detect hint fallout and autotune hints per node.
acceptance_criteria: - Deployment of feature-flagged policy with end-to-end integration tests. - A/B on staging for 48h shows: overall throughput >= +6%, latency-sensitive tenant 95th <= baseline+5% and ideally improved. - Observability: new dashboard panels (coalesce_rate, kernel_hint_mismatch, tenant_budget_utilization) wired to console and alerts. - Docs: RFC and operator playbook (rollback steps) published in Confluence. - PRs merged: runtime arbiter changes + kernel hint plumbing + console dashboards.
